reason: Re-rendered the AnlBV Anhang chart (BGBl. I 2005 p. 2297) myself. The grey dashed 'Grenze des Gebietes ausserhalb des Hoheitsgebietes' runs from about 54 04N 007 20E south-west to about 53 49N 006 15E, then east to the territorial sea near the Ems. It crosses the Terschelling-German Bight lanes at about 006 15E to 006 20E, which agrees with the record (006 16E to 006 22E). The current AnlBV Anlage (gesetze-im-internet.de) confirms Nr. 1.17 (the Innere Deutsche Bucht is defined by the Anhang), Nr. 3.1 (report to Verkehrszentrale German Bight Traffic on VHF 79 or 80 at 007 10E or 54 20N) and Nr. 5.1 (traffic monitored under maritime traffic safety). A secondary source (findaport, commercial, undated) gives a German Bight Traffic reporting point at longitude 006 22.8E for ships using this TSS. That independently supports the boundary position; it is not Tier 1. ELWIS and the WSA Weser-Jade-Nordsee pages are live and list German Bight Traffic (Wilhelmshaven, VHF 16/79/80) as current. Reporting classification: SeeSchStrO s.58 reports go to the Verkehrszentrale (quote confirmed on ELWIS), and AnlBV 3.1 goes to German Bight Traffic, so they count as VTS reporting. WETREP's North Sea limit (Belgium/Netherlands border to UK coast at 52 12N) excludes the area. No other IMO Part I system applies. No official German source giving the VTS limits as coordinates could be retrieved: the BSH VTS Guide Germany PDF on bsh.de is only the 3-page contents list. The chart-grid precision caveat therefore stays, but partial coverage is secure.

The classification (VTS only, partial) is upheld, but the stated extent of coverage is probably too narrow and should be reworded. On the chart I confirm that the Innere Deutsche Bucht (VHF 80) boundary crosses the GBWA lanes at about 007 19E, so only the eastern end (to about 007 25E) is inside the VHF 80 area. However, the AnlBV itself requires ships to report to German Bight Traffic on VHF 79 or 80 at 007 10E, west of that boundary. Secondary sources (findaport) also describe a German Bight Traffic 'western area' on VHF 79, with a reporting point at lightbuoy GW/B, 54 10.42N 006 54.00E, on GBWA itself. So the German Bight Traffic VTS area probably reaches further west along GBWA than 007 18E. The VHF 80 Innere Deutsche Bucht is a statutory definition for AnlBV purposes and is not necessarily the whole VTS area. Suggested change: keep 'partial', but say German Bight Traffic covers at least the eastern section (VHF 80 area east of about 007 19E), with probable western-area (VHF 79) coverage to about 006 54E or beyond (not confirmed by a Tier 1 source). The remaining western length in the Dutch EEZ lies outside any German VTS. Also keep the German North Sea Traffic (Cuxhaven, Aeussere Deutsche Bucht) lead open. The reporting classification is correct: AnlBV 3.1 goes to the VTS, AnlBV 6 is routeing, and there is no Part I system (WETREP excluded).

The current AnlBV Anlage Nr. 8 wording ('Lotsenversetzposition im Verkehrstrennungsgebiet "Jade Approach" ... 5 Seemeilen noerdlich der Tonne "TG 18"') is confirmed. On the re-rendered Anhang chart, the Jade Approach lanes (about 53 55N to 54 00N, 007 30E to 007 50E) lie well inside both the VHF 80 arc and the dashed boundary, and adjoin the territorial sea. German Bight Traffic and Jade Traffic (Verkehrszentrale Wilhelmshaven) are both listed as current on ELWIS and WSA pages. The reporting classification is correct, and no IMO Part I system applies.

The BAnz AT 31.01.2014 B7 wording is confirmed. Nr. 29.1.2.1 reads 'Cuxhaven fuer den Bereich vom Tonne Elbe bis zum Tonnenpaar 53, 54/Reede ueber UKW-Kanal 71 ... Cuxhaven Elbe Traffic'. Nr. 29.1.4 gives the outbound report at Tonne Elbe on VHF 80 to German Bight Traffic. On the chart, the Elbe approach lies deep inside the VHF 80 area. Cuxhaven Elbe Traffic (VHF 16/71) and German Bight Traffic are both listed as current on ELWIS, and the WSA Elbe-Nordsee page confirms that Cuxhaven covers the Elbeansteuerung. Both sectors belong to the German coastal VTS, so full coverage holds whatever the sector split. I did not verify later amendments to Nr. 29.1. The researcher already flags this, and it affects only the sector hand-over. The reporting classification is correct, and no Part I system applies.

The ABP Humber Estuary Services page (humber.com, live, official statutory harbour authority) confirms the limit text: Easington Church 53 39.02N 000 06.90E, 086 degrees to 53 40N 000 30E, 180 degrees to 53 30N 000 30E, 262 degrees to Donna Nook 53 28.40N 000 09.23E. It also confirms that the system is compulsory for sea-going vessels and that Outer Binks, Outer Sea Reach and Outer Rosse Reach are reporting points. I re-tested all COLREG.2/Circ.60 vertices. The easternmost is 000 22.95E, inside the 000 30E line. The northern line at 000 21.24E to 000 22.49E lies at about 53 39.6N to 53 39.7N, north of points 36 and 37 (53 38.70N and 53 38.35N). The southern line gives 53 29.35N at point 29 and 53 29.29N at point 28, both inside. Point 30 (53 29.19N 000 19.97E) falls between the endpoint interpolation (about 53 29.23N) and the 262-degree rhumb (about 53 29.16N), so it lies on the limit within charting precision. Full coverage stands. No post-2009 Humber TSS amendment was found. The Part I check is also correct: WETREP's UK east coast limits are 52 12N and 58 30N, and the Humber lies between them, outside WETREP.
